headline: GOLDSEEK: HERE'S WHERE GOLD AND SILVER STAND — POST-WARSH TECHNICAL RESET WITH SUPPORT AT $4,577 GOLD AND $64 SILVER EMA; BULLS WATCHING NEXT MACRO TRIGGERS
snippet: Published August 30, GoldSeek's latest summary gives retail investors the clearest post-Jackson Hole read on where gold and silver actually stand technically after last week's Warsh shock. Gold spot is consolidating near $4,580–$4,610 following Friday's volatility; the immediate technical floor is the 20-day EMA around $4,460, with $4,577 the level bulls must hold heading into Monday's COMEX open. Silver stabilised at approximately $66–$69 after the 4.5% single-session drop on Warsh's 'work to do' comment, with the 50-day EMA near $64.65 as the next meaningful support if the dollar continues to strengthen into September data. The bullish structural case — six consecutive annual silver deficits, central bank gold demand at a 62-year high, gold miners delivering their best monthly performance on record in August — is described as intact and unchanged by rate policy. The critical question the article frames heading into September: do the five upcoming data prints (JOLTS, ADP, PCE, ISM Services, NFP) push September hike odds above 50% or compress them back toward zero? The answer determines whether $4,600 is the floor or ceiling for October.

headline: GOLD FIELDS CEO: GHANA IS TREATING MINERS AS AN 'EASY TARGET' — H1 PROFIT SOARS 81% BUT TARKWA LEASE RENEWAL THROWS SHADOW OVER AFRICA'S GOLD
snippet: Gold Fields (JSE: GFI; NYSE: GFI) released its H1 2026 interim results on August 25, with headline earnings surging 81% and the company raising its dividend — but CEO Mike Fraser used the results call to issue an unusually direct critique of Ghana's mining policies, saying Accra is treating the sector as 'an easy target' for government revenue. The Tarkwa gold mine — Ghana's largest, accounting for roughly one-fifth of Gold Fields' global production — has five mining leases expiring in April 2027. Gold Fields submitted a 20-year renewal application in November 2025 with a commercial proposal in July 2026 and has yet to receive a formal government response. Ghana simultaneously hiked royalties on gold to as much as 12% from 5% and set a December 2026 deadline for foreign majors including Newmont, AngloGold Ashanti, and Zijin to shift surface mining operations to 100%-Ghanaian-owned contractors under threat of sanction. The Tarkwa risk comes as Gold Fields' South Africa Deep operations and Cerro Corona in Peru deliver record margins at $4,600+ gold — a stark contrast between asset quality and the jurisdictional uncertainty that could impair the mine's contribution to guidance. For retail investors tracking jurisdiction risk in West Africa: Tarkwa-style lease uncertainty creates a valuation floor question for any company with material Ghana exposure.

headline: GHANA GIVES NEWMONT, ANGLOGOLD AND ZIJIN UNTIL DECEMBER TO SHIFT MINING OPS TO LOCAL CONTRACTORS — RESOURCE NATIONALISM AT AFRICA'S LARGEST GOLD PRODUCER
snippet: Ghana's Minerals Commission has formally directed Newmont, AngloGold Ashanti, and Zijin Mining to transition their surface mining operations to 100%-Ghanaian-owned contract mining firms by December 2026 or face regulatory sanctions, according to letters sent to the companies. The policy reflects Ghana's broader push to deepen local ownership of gold mining — Africa's largest gold producer by output — as the government simultaneously raised royalties from 5% to as high as 12% and restricted mining lease bids to Ghanaian-owned companies. Most large operators already comply with the local-contractor rules; Newmont, AngloGold, and Zijin are among the small group still operating with their own workforce and have separately requested compliance extensions. The Minerals Commission's hardening stance — coming as Gold Fields' CEO publicly branded the government an 'easy target' policy maker — signals that Ghana's resource-nationalism trajectory is accelerating rather than moderating, regardless of the current gold price. For junior investors evaluating West Africa as an exploration jurisdiction: the combination of rising royalties, lease tenure uncertainty, and forced operational restructuring represents a material increase in country risk that is not yet fully reflected in the comparable-transaction premiums used to value early-stage Ghana exploration.

headline: VR RESOURCES DRILLS 317m AT 0.77% CuEq FROM SURFACE AT NEW BOSTON NEVADA PORPHYRY — SHARES SURGE 148% ON POLYMETALLIC DISCOVERY INSIDE 881m HOLE
snippet: VR Resources Limited (TSX.V: VRR) reported geochemical assay results from drill hole NB26-003 at its New Boston Moly-Tungsten-Copper-Silver-Zinc porphyry-skarn project in west-central Nevada on August 26, 2026, triggering a 147.92% single-day share price gain on volume of over 8 million shares — one of the largest single-session gains for a TSX-V junior in 2026. The 881-metre hole returned near-continuous mineralization across the full drill length in molybdenum, copper, tungsten, silver, and zinc within complex polyphase stockwork veining, with highlights including 317 metres at 0.77% copper equivalent (CuEq) starting from surface, overlying 419 metres of 0.48% CuEq beneath, and a new diorite porphyry intrusion containing 31 metres at 0.98% CuEq — the highest-grade zone in the system. The New Boston project is located off Highway 95, a major transportation corridor, in a favourable permitting jurisdiction with no existing resource estimate — meaning this intercept is a true first-pass discovery, not a resource expansion. At copper above $6.50 per pound, a near-surface 317-metre bulk-tonnage CuEq intercept of this scale in western Nevada is a category of discovery that historically triggers rapid institutional attention and follow-up programs.

headline: COPPER RETREATS FROM $6.7775/lb ALL-TIME RECORD AS COMEX SQUEEZE EASES — KAMOA-KAKULA STILL OFFLINE BUT EXCHANGE INVENTORY BUILD TAKES EDGE OFF
snippet: COMEX copper for September delivery touched $6.7775 per pound on August 26 — a fresh all-time nominal high — before retreating 1.6% to $6.6070 by late morning in New York as a build-up in exchange inventories signalled the most acute phase of the short-squeeze was easing. The underlying structural supply deficit remains unchanged: Zijin Mining has warned that flooding at the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex in the DRC could cut its share of production by up to 57,000 tonnes in 2026, and the Sandvik underground equipment order for Kakula (announced August 28) signals the restart is Q4 2026 at the earliest. Indonesia's failure to replace a key smelter that went offline earlier in August added a second supply shock to the market. The technical retreat from record highs is a normal pattern in commodity markets following a positioning extreme — copper has surged approximately 15% year-to-date as traders ship metal into the US ahead of tariff deadlines, draining stockpiles elsewhere while mine supply remains constrained. For junior copper explorers: the COMEX record at $6.78 is the market's clearest signal that advanced-stage copper projects in low-geopolitical-risk jurisdictions remain among the most valuable undeveloped assets in the ground globally.

headline: CATL JIANXIAWO MINE STAYS SHUT PENDING ENVIRONMENTAL PERMIT — LITHIUM REBOUNDS TO 153,000 CNY/T AS WORLD'S LARGEST LEPIDOLITE MINE KEEPS 60K-TONNE LCE OFFLINE
snippet: CATL's Jianxiawo lithium mine in Yichun, Jiangxi — the world's largest lepidolite deposit at 2.7 million tonnes of lithium — remains suspended as of August 28, 2026, with the company's safety production permit secured June 29 but a new environmental impact assessment (EIA) still pending final approval after public consultation closed July 27. Caixin Global reported Yichun authorities confirmed the site remains idle with no active ore processing or transport. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence estimates a prolonged shutdown puts approximately 60,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) supply at risk in Jiangxi province — a figure equivalent to roughly 5% of 2026 global LCE supply. Lithium carbonate on the Guangzhou Futures Exchange rose to 153,000 CNY/T (approximately $22,500/tonne) on August 28, up 0.33% on the day and 11% from July lows as the stalled restart kept a supply-side floor under a market that spent much of midsummer pricing oversupply. For lithium battery-metals investors tracking TSX-V and ASX explorers: the Jianxiawo EIA delay is the most material single-asset supply catalyst in the lithium market heading into Q4 2026, and its resolution — in either direction — will move lithium carbonate prices by 10–20% within days of announcement.

headline: GOLDSEEK: CAN GDX HIT NEW ALL-TIME HIGHS BY YEAR END? — GOLD MINERS' MARGIN EXPANSION THESIS INTACT AFTER BEST AUGUST ON RECORD
snippet: GoldSeek's recent technical analysis of the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) argues that new all-time highs by year-end remain plausible given the fundamental backdrop: gold miners posted their strongest calendar month in recorded history in August 2026 (+43% for the MSCI global gold miners index), and producer fundamentals have rarely been stronger — net cash positions, rising dividends, expanding free cash flow at $4,600 gold, and all-in sustaining costs rising far more slowly than the gold price. GDX printed new all-time highs in early 2026 before the distribution and consolidation phase through Q2; the post-August re-acceleration has recovered substantial ground. The key technical question the article frames: is the August surge the final capitulation wave of a momentum extreme, or the early phase of a multi-quarter advance as generalist capital rotates into the sector? The article's base case is that the sector's fundamental margin expansion — gold prices compressing 3–4 years of cost inflation in a single year — is structural and will not reverse quickly, making dips within the context of the 2026 bull market accumulation opportunities for investors positioned ahead of the junior-explorer rotation that historically follows senior producer re-ratings by 3–6 months.

headline: KAZATOMPROM H1 2026: REVENUE +9% TO KZT 718B, URANIUM AVERAGED $85.98/LB — BUT TQZ ACID PLANT PUSHED TO 2027-28, TIGHTENING SUPPLY WINDOW
snippet: Kazatomprom — the world's largest uranium producer — reported its H1 2026 financial results on August 21, with consolidated revenue rising 9% year-on-year to KZT 718 billion, driven by a 24% increase in the average weekly uranium spot price to USD 85.98 per pound versus the same period in 2025. Total uranium production rose 9% to 13,291 tonnes (100% basis). However, net profit fell 9% to KZT 240.4 billion, impacted by higher foreign exchange losses, finance costs, and cost of sales. The more significant long-term signal: the TQZ sulphuric acid plant — a critical input for Kazatomprom's in-situ leach operations — has been delayed from the original 2026 commissioning target to Q3 2027–Q1 2028 after construction halted for paleontological specimen recovery and project documentation approval delays. The TQZ delay is not immediately impacting 2026 uranium production, as sulphuric acid supplies for 2026 are estimated to be stable. But it compresses the post-2026 supply ramp that the uranium market had been counting on to buffer the supply-demand gap as data-centre nuclear demand and reactor restarts accelerate globally. For uranium investors watching NexGen's Rook I construction and Paladin's Langer Heinrich restart: Kazatomprom's inability to scale TQZ on schedule is a structural tailwind for Western uranium producers with production in the 2028–2030 window.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GOLD AND SILVER STAGING POWERFUL BREAKOUTS — ANALYSTS SEE TECHNICAL CONFIRMATION OF THE BULL RUN ENTERING ITS MOST EXPLOSIVE PHASE
snippet: GoldSeek's recent breakout analysis argues that both gold and silver have completed the technical pattern formation necessary to confirm the current bull market as a genuine multi-year advance rather than a cyclical momentum trade. Gold's August surge above $4,500 and its ability to hold that level even after the Warsh Jackson Hole shock — which knocked gold only temporarily below $4,600 before buyers re-emerged — signals that the price level has been re-anchored to a new structural base. Silver's failure to hold the $72 breakout is characterised in the analysis not as a reversal but as a retest of the breakout zone, with the 46.3-million-ounce structural annual deficit functioning as a demand floor that becomes visible each time the paper market applies a short-term discount. The article highlights the historical pattern: the most explosive phase of a precious metals bull market tends to occur after miners outperform the metal for a sustained period — which is now occurring, with GDX and GDXJ both having delivered 3x–4x gold's monthly percentage gain in August. For retail investors evaluating position sizing in junior mining: the breakout confirmation framework suggests the optimal entry window for quality junior explorers historically runs 6–12 months after the senior producer re-rating phase begins, which August 2026 appears to be.

headline: PRECIOUS METALS WEEK IN REVIEW: GOLD HOLDS ABOVE $4,600, SILVER AT $69, AS WARSH HAWKISHNESS TESTS THE BULL BUT DOESN'T BREAK IT
snippet: The Precious Metals Week in Review for August 28, 2026 frames the week's price action as a controlled retreat within a sustained bull trend rather than a reversal: gold spot closed near $4,608 per ounce on Friday after touching $4,656 mid-week and absorbing Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole address, which pushed September rate hike odds from approximately 31% to 38% but failed to break gold below the $4,500 level that had served as resistance-turned-support. Silver settled around $69, down from its $72+ pre-Warsh high but above the 50-day EMA support zone that retail and institutional accumulators have treated as a reload point throughout 2026. Drivers of the week's resilience include central bank buying estimated at 288.9 tonnes in Q2 2026 (a 62% year-on-year increase), continued physical demand from Asia despite the rate hawkishness, and the observation that Warsh's first substantive public communication as Fed Chair revealed a policy hawkishness that markets had not fully priced. Gold is up approximately 13% in August alone; silver is up approximately 14%. Both metals have now compounded their YTD returns well beyond any major equity index as of August 28, 2026.
